dedupe_keys.name: river dataset as a potential fluvial transportation network for healthcare access in the amazon region

description: River dataset as a potential fluvial transportation network for healthcare access in the Amazon region is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Thiago Augusto Hernandes Rocha et al. Remote areas, such as the Amazon Forest, face unique geographical challenges of transportation-based access to health services. As transportation to healthcare in most of the Amazon Forest is only possible by rivers routes, any travel time and travel distance estimation is limited by the lack of data sources containing rivers as potential transportation routes. Coverage: not stated; published in 2023. Formats: Shapefile. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 184369902 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support emergency-service and public-facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
